props.title: Agnes of God

sections.content: Agnes of God (1985) stands as a haunting exploration of faith, science, and psychological trauma through the lens of a disturbing murder investigation. Director Norman Jewison crafts a claustrophobic chamber drama reminiscent of Doubt (2008), but with sharper psychological edges. The film pits Jane Fonda's rational court psychiatrist against Meg Tilly's innocent nun Agnes and Anne Bancroft's protective Mother Superior, creating a taut triangle of conflicting beliefs. Like The Exorcist (1973), it grapples with questions of divine intervention versus mental illness, but trades supernatural horror for psychological complexity.

sections.content: The film exemplifies a wave of 1980s religious-themed dramas that questioned institutional faith, alongside works like Mass Appeal (1984) and True Confessions (1981). Jewison's direction emphasizes stark contrasts - both visual and thematic - between the sterile modern world and the ancient traditions of the convent. The cinematography by Sven Nykvist (Ingmar Bergman's longtime collaborator) creates a dreamlike atmosphere that enhances the film's exploration of memory, truth, and belief.

Meg Tilly's Oscar-nominated performance as Agnes showcases the complex intersection of innocence and trauma that would influence later films like The Magdalene Sisters (2002) and Novitiate (2017). The interrogation scenes between Fonda and Tilly are masterclasses in psychological tension, echoing the intensity of Girl, Interrupted (1999) while maintaining a uniquely spiritual dimension. movies.title: The Magdalene Sisters
movies.slug: The story of three young women confined to a Magdalene Asylum in 1960s Ireland

sections.content: The power dynamics between the three lead women reflect broader themes about institutional control and female autonomy that would later be explored in films like Black Narcissus (1947) and The Little Hours (2017). Anne Bancroft's Mother Miriam Ruth serves as a complex antagonist who, like Meryl Streep's character in Doubt, believes she's protecting her charge while potentially enabling darker truths to remain hidden.
